name: PBEKeySpec
protocol: new PBEKeySpec(char[], byte[], int, int) ; clearPassword()
important_note: The verified canonical CrySL source directly declares SPEC javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec and observes PBEKeySpec constructors plus clearPassword(). The required javax.crypto.interfaces.PBEKey type is included to satisfy the requested CrySL-style PBEKey naming target, but the attempted canonical PBEKey.crysl URL returned HTTP 404 and must not be treated as verified direct evidence that the corpus rule declares PBEKey.

events.name: construct_with_password_salt_iterations_key_length
events.condition: Observed when a four-argument PBEKeySpec constructor invocation is present. The canonical CrySL predicates are satisfied only with statically associated iterationCount >= 10000, a password not typed as java.lang.String, a non-hard-coded password, and randomized[salt] evidence. Observing the call alone does not establish those predicates.

events.name: clear_password
events.condition: Observed when clearPassword() is invoked on the relevant PBEKeySpec instance. In the verified rule protocol it follows permitted four-argument construction; observing this substring does not prove receiver identity, all-path execution, or clearing of external password-array copies.

events.name: forbidden_password_only_constructor
events.condition: Observed when the one-argument PBEKeySpec(char[]) constructor is invoked. The verified CrySL source lists this overload as FORBIDDEN; a salt and iteration-count predicate cannot be established through this overload because those arguments are absent.

events.name: forbidden_password_salt_iterations_constructor
events.condition: Observed when the three-argument PBEKeySpec(char[], byte[], int) constructor is invoked. The verified CrySL source lists this overload as FORBIDDEN, although JDK documentation provides it for fixed-key-size PBE ciphers; the CrySL protocol permits only the four-argument constructor event.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: A PBEKeySpec construction proves that SecretKeyFactory.generateSecret(...) was called or that a derived key was actually produced.
A PBEKeySpec construction proves the KDF, PRF, provider, cipher, key length actually used, or the document-encryption format.
The reported value 10000 proves a runtime call occurred; the representative message expressly says the hardening candidate was not executed.
The reported value 10000 violates the verified CrySL constraint; that source specifies iterationCount >= 10000, so exactly 10000 meets that baseline.
A salt byte array is randomized merely because it is non-null, non-empty, or named salt; randomized[salt] requires provenance evidence.

clearPassword() clears the caller's original char[] or every copy returned by getPassword(); documented behavior concerns PBEKeySpec's internal password copy, and returned copies remain the caller's responsibility to erase.

The verified CrySL source directly governs javax.crypto.interfaces.PBEKey. It directly declares javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec; inclusion of PBEKey reflects the required naming target and API relationship, not a verified PBEKey.crysl declaration.
semantic_scope: This is a static protocol-and-predicate context for javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec: selected constructor overloads, clearPassword(), an iteration-count floor, password type/source restrictions, and salt-randomization evidence. The representative finding narrows this to other.de.stanetz.jpencconverter.JavaPasswordbasedCryption.createKeyFromPassword, where V001 and U001 reportedly supply 10000 as the PBEKeySpec iteration argument for password-derived document-encryption keys. No implementation, call graph, or execution trace was supplied.

detector_semantics.claim: The supplied message reports a static hardening candidate for a PBEKeySpec iteration argument of 10000 in JavaPasswordbasedCryption.createKeyFromPassword. It explicitly characterizes the candidate as not executed and recommends calibrating a stronger work factor only for a new format version.
predicates: Verified canonical CrySL predicate: neverTypeOf[password, java.lang.String].
Representative-finding predicate as reported: V001 and U001 both resolve to 10000 for the PBEKeySpec iteration argument.
limitations: No repository source, call graph, data-flow trace, or runtime trace was provided for the reported class and method.
The message does not identify the SecretKeyFactory algorithm, provider, PRF, salt origin, key length, cipher, or persisted-format compatibility constraints.
The verified CrySL source establishes a minimum of 10000, not that 10000 is adequate for every password-derived-key deployment.

documented_behavior: javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec represents a user-chosen password usable with password-based encryption.
Its four-argument constructor accepts password, salt, iteration count, and desired derived-key length for variable-key-size PBE ciphers; password and salt are cloned.
clearPassword() clears PBEKeySpec's internal password copy.
The related javax.crypto.interfaces.PBEKey interface exposes password, salt, and iteration count for a PBE key.
preconditions: For the three- and four-argument JDK constructors, salt must not be null or empty.
For the three- and four-argument JDK constructors, iterationCount must be positive.
For the four-argument JDK constructor, keyLength must be positive.
After clearPassword(), getPassword() throws IllegalStateException according to the JDK documentation.
The JDK API permits a null password by treating it as an empty char[]; the CrySL rule separately disallows a password value typed as java.lang.String.
unknowns: Whether the reported code uses PBKDF2, legacy PKCS #5 PBE, PKCS #12 PBE, or another provider-specific SecretKeyFactory algorithm.
Whether V001 and U001 are literal constants, configuration values, version fields, tainted values, or detector-internal symbolic labels.
Whether the salt is freshly generated per protected document and retained for decryption.
Whether clearPassword() is reached for every constructed PBEKeySpec instance.

security_semantics.detector_claim: The representative message treats the reported 10000-iteration construction as a CWE-916-oriented static hardening candidate, not evidence of a runtime exploit or a confirmed CrySL-rule violation.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: No runtime security conclusion follows from the finding alone. Such a conclusion requires evidence of the executed KDF and provider, resolved iteration count, password properties, salt generation and uniqueness, derived-key use, and applicable format/version behavior.

Show the expression or value flow supplying password, salt, iterationCount, and keyLength.
For canonical CrySL compliance, establish iterationCount >= 10000, non-String and non-hard-coded password handling, and randomized salt provenance.
If asserting a direct PBEKey rule target, provide a source declaring SPEC javax.crypto.interfaces.PBEKey; the attempted PBEKey.crysl URL was missing.

Identify the resolved SecretKeyFactory algorithm and provider behavior.
Capture the effective iteration count, salt bytes and provenance, derived-key length, and whether secret generation's result is used.
Establish object identity and path coverage showing clearPassword() is invoked on the constructed PBEKeySpec after use.
compatibility: Identify the format-version fields or serialized metadata represented by V001 and U001.
Determine whether documents created with the current format must remain decryptable and where KDF parameters are stored.
Verify that encrypting and decrypting code agree on KDF algorithm, salt, iteration count, and derived-key length.
Establish migration or version-selection behavior; none is established by the supplied finding.

known_false_positive_shapes: A policy labels exactly 10000 as weak even though the verified CrySL rule accepts it because its written condition is >= 10000.
The static analysis sees a dead, test-only, unsupported-version, or otherwise unexecuted constructor path.
Salt randomization is provided by an approved helper or external boundary whose provenance is unavailable to the analysis.
A non-literal secure password source loses provenance through intermediate representations and is classified as hard-coded or String-typed.
clearPassword() occurs through an alias, helper, exceptional-cleanup path, or language interoperation that the detector does not connect to the constructed instance.
The message labels the use document encryption, but the specification is later used for another purpose or key generation fails before use.
unknowns: Why the consumer-facing identifier is PBEKeySpec while the requested naming convention requires a PBEKey target: the available verified corpus source is PBEKeySpec.crysl and directly declares SPEC javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec.
Whether a separate historical, generated, or project-local PBEKeySpec specification maps that identifier to javax.crypto.interfaces.PBEKey.

detector_examples.message: Static hardening candidate (not executed): PBEKeySpec receives 10000 iterations from both V001 and U001 for password-derived document encryption keys (CWE-916); calibrate a stronger work factor for a new format version.
